title: Abundance and Distribution of Tintinnids in the Mangrove‐Associated Coastal Ecosystem of South Andaman
content:
ABSTRACT

A four-month study (January–April 2025) was conducted to assess the physicochemical variables influencing the tintinnid community in three distinct regions: the Bay Region (Sippighat), the Eastern Region (Burmanallah and Corbyn′s Cove), and the Western Region (Manjery) in the coastal waters of South Andaman. Surface water samples were collected from the proximal zone of the mangrove to assess the environmental and biological variables. A total of 21 tintinnid species belonging to seven genera were recorded across these regions. The Bay Region (Sippighat) had the highest species richness and diversity, while the least diversity was observed in the Western Region (Manjery). Spearman's rank correlation showed that temperature and pH had relatively strong (though weak) associations with tintinnid abundance compared with the other environmental variables, but these associations were not statistically significant. K-dominance analysis revealed a more even species-abundance structure in the Bay Region. Whittaker's beta diversity was highest between the Bay and Western regions, indicating the most distinct assemblages there.
